 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 16-07-2023 at about 12.00 p.m., the petitioner was crossing the Kasavanahalli main road, in order to go to M. Syphony Apartment for house work, with due care and caution, by observing all traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 70-H-1578 came in rash and negligent manner,
with high speed, endangering to human life and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was working as house worker and she was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

But, due to accidental injuries,
she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Bellanduru Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 April, 2025

3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The the respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that,
the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-70-H-1578 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the motorcycle in the alleged accident.

It has contended that, the insured vehicle had no fitness certificate as on the date of alleged accident, the motorcycle in question did not involve in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner.
The petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police have created false records and story about the manner and involvement of motorcycle to get compensation and has lodged a false complaint.

Further it is contended that, at the time of accident the motorcycle was driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

The accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was crossing the road without having proper look out at the vehicular movements on the road and without noticing oncoming vehicles and she was crossing the road carelessly and caused the accident.
The accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and not due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

Further he has contended that, he was traveling to his home from the work situated at Sri Sai Nilaya, Prashanth Layout, Hoodi, K.R. Puram, Bengaluru, on 14-01-2023 in his motorcycle of the make and model TVS N-Torq bearing Reg. No.KA-70-H- 1578, cautiously, by following the traffic rules and regulations, abiding all the safety rules imposed in the Kasavanahalli Main Road, he was holding valid driving licence bearing No.KA7020190007758, valid till 18-07-2039 and valid insurance.
The said motorcycle was insured by respondent No.1 company i.e., M/s. Liberty General Insurance Company Limited.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner suddenly tried to cross the road from left side, carelessly and without any safety signs, neglecting all the traffic rules and regulations.
He was riding his motorcycle by following the traffic rules and regulations and tried his best to avoid the impact and also stopped the vehicle immediately to avoid the accident.
Despite his due effort, he failed to resist the incident and due to negligence of the petitioner the accident was inevitable.
He shifted the petitioner to the Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru and paid the bill of the hospital, with respect to first aid treatment taken by the petitioner.

Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-70-H-1578 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained acute subdural haematoma in left cerebral convexity with mass effect and midline shift,
left subfalcine and uncal herniation, undisplaced fracture of left parietal bone and left temporal bone and for the said injuries she has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.1.
As per Ex.P.1, the date of birth of the petitioner is 13-09-1996.
The accident has taken place on 16-07-2023 at about 12.00 P.M. Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident wad 27 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered acute Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. 7 subdural haematoma in left cerebral convexity with mass effect and midline shift, left subfalcine and uncal herniation, undisplaced fracture of left parietal bone and left temporal bone and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. for removal of brain haemorrhage - Left FTP decompressive craniectomy and evacuation of acute SDH under GA.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent neurological disability to the extent of 45% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.12 discharge summary, Ex.P.17 and 18 inpatient records (total 2), Ex.P.19 OPD record with clinical notes, Ex.P.21 assessment report with work sheet, Ex.P.22 CT brain report, Ex.P.23 CT Scan films (total 7), Ex.P.24 CT scan report and Ex.P.25 outpatient slips (total 2) also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
He has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, he has clearly admitted that, except the head injury the petitioner has not sustained fracture of any other part of her body, the injuries caused to the brain of the petitioner is healed with scar.
Further he has admitted that, the clotting of the blood has been removed by conducting surgery.
Further, he has admitted that, he has not assessed the IQ of the petitioner.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 16-07-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 25-10- 2024, which is after lapse of one year and three months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has clearly admitted that, he has not assessed the functional disability of the petitioner.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, the petitioner herself has stepped into witness box and depose her evidence.
The petitioner has answered all the questions and suggestions put to her in the cross- examination very smartly and correctly.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified
. Hence, in the instant case the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as house worker and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to the accidental injuries she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

She has not produced any document to show that,
before accident she was working as house worker and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10784262/
8 and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 27 years is 17.

ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.10,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 85 medical bills, as per Ex.P.15 and Ex.P26.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.10,31,516/- towards medical expenses.

Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,31,516/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., acute subdural haematoma in left cerebral convexity with mass effect and midline shift, left subfalcine and uncal herniation, undisplaced fracture of left parietal bone and left temporal bone and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. for removal of brain haemorrhage - Left FTP decompressive craniectomy and evacuation of acute SDH under GA.
As per Ex.P.12 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 11 days, from 16-07- 2023 to 26-07-2023, in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
She has also undergone surgery i.e. for removal of brain haemorrhage - Left FTP decompressive craniectomy and evacuation of acute SDH under GA.
Further, as per P.W.2 the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges: As per Ex.P.12 discharge summary
, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 11 days in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 11 =
Rs.11,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.12 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 11 days in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs. 800 x 11 = Rs.8,800/-
is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Shivanahalli, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place on Kasavanahalli main road, in front of H.M. Symphony Apartment,
Sarjapura main road, Bengaluru City and she has taken treatment at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.

Taking into consideration the distance in between the place of accident and the above hospitals,
compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 11 days as in-patient at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 27 years and unfortunately she has sustained acute subdural haematoma in left cerebral convexity with mass effect and midline shift, left subfalcine and uncal herniation, undisplaced fracture of left parietal bone and left temporal bone.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body.

ix) Future medical expenses:
There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident in question.
Further, the P.W.2 has not stated anything with regard to requirement of any further treatment to the petitioner or future medical expenses.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 6,32,400-00 2.
Medical expenses 10,31,516-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 11,000-00
5. Food and nourishment 8,800-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses -Nil-

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.17,79,716/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

To establish the same the petitioner has Jayanthi P D Joshi Alias Janaki Joshi vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10784262/

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 has also produced his driving licence, which is marked as Ex.R.1.

As per the said documents, the rider/respondent No.2 of offending vehicle by name Renwil Dsouza S/o Ronald Boniface Dsouza was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA70-20190007758 to drive the said vehicle, as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was insured by respondent No.1 insurance company, vide Policy No.2012-500203-19-8008052-00-003, valid from 25-01-2020 to 24-01-2025.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-70-H-1578 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.17,79,716/-
from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.17,79,716/- (Rupees seventeen lakh seventy nine thousand seven hundred and sixteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as FD in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who was the rider and owner of the offending vehicle at the time of accident, there is no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report,
the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending scooter and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the given facts and circumstances of the case,
it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-70-H- 1578.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to negligence of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on her part in the cause of accident.

the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified
. Hence, in the instant case the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
